Fixture: 10_modular_palette_128x128_lossless.jxl
128x128 RGB, mathematically lossless, effort 7 -- aims to trigger the
modular palette transform

Purpose
-------
Targets slices 5/6/7 (modular decoding, frame headers, end-to-end lossless).
Exactly 4 distinct RGB colours (black, white, red, blue) laid out as four
64x64 solid quadrants -- a shape deliberately chosen because the modular
palette transform activates when an image has few distinct colours, and a
low colour count is exactly what a real "flat cartoon/UI" source looks like.
-e 7 gives the encoder its default full effort budget to consider the
transform (compare 09, which uses -e 3 for the RCT case).

128x128 is single-group. It targets palette-transform correctness, not
tiling.

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 7
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_palette_128x128.ppm  (49167 bytes)
                sha256 21105db1d9c0fa649fce9349ac08e26947f375783f0d403c92e0931dba82f06b
                Synthetic, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was
                used, converted, or consulted. 128x128 8-bit RGB (PPM P6),
                a 2x2 grid of solid 64x64 blocks, top-left to bottom-right:
                  (0,0)=black (0,0,0)     (255,0)=white (255,255,255)
                  (0,255)=red (237,28,36) (255,255)=blue (0,114,255)
                Only 4 distinct RGB triplets across the whole 16384-pixel
                image -- deliberately low colour cardinality to give the
                palette transform something to find.

  Fixture:      67 bytes
                sha256 0ec547c7e942bf5f7460799d405b2c1b8968e0f861f7b4f948110b1d8203f0b2

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PPM byte-identical to the source (checked on every run
of tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh). Classified by `jpxl info` (jpxl-cli) as
a recognized "naked codestream". 67 bytes for a 128x128x3 (49152-sample)
image -- circumstantial evidence that *some* aggressive redundancy-removal
transform fired (a naive per-pixel modular encode of 4 flat blocks would
still cost far more than 67 bytes without one), consistent with the palette
transform being engaged, but not confirmed by name.

Modular features engaged
-------------------------
Not independently confirmed by name -- cjxl printed "Modular, lossless" at
encode time and nothing more specific; jxlinfo is not built in this
checkout; djxl -v / -v -v print no per-feature detail for this stream. The
extreme compression ratio (67 bytes / 49167-byte source) is suggestive of
the palette transform given the source's 4-colour design, but that is an
inference from the fixture's own construction, not a tool-confirmed fact.
See 07_modular_gray_8x8_lossless.jxl.txt for the general caveat.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
